# RTO-6 State Model Review

## Summary

The draft has the right state names, but it is not testable or safe as written. It has five main problems:

1. **The thermal oxidizer cannot destroy fumes reliably under this model.** Fumes stay in PROCESS when TT-601 falls below the temperature needed for destruction.
2. **XV-602 is never controlled.** Without it, the model can block the CL-6 exhaust (both valves closed) or send fumes to the stack untreated (both valves open).
3. **Burner management logic is mixed into the state model.** Purge and light-off belong to the BMS under NFPA 86, not to the BPCS state model.
4. **FAULT has no exit and no defined response.**
5. **Numbers are written in the prose.** They should live in the setpoint list.

## Findings

| ID | Location | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-01 | Whole model | No requirement IDs or test methods. Nothing is traceable to FAT. | Give every state and transition an FR-RTO6-NNN ID and a test method. |
| F-02 | PURGE, HEAT-UP, PROCESS, COOL-DOWN | Numbers in prose (5 min, 760 C, 200 C). | Move them to the setpoint list. Reference them by name. |
| F-03 | One 760 C value | One value is used for two jobs: the READY permissive and the PROCESS control action. With no deadband, the model will chatter at the boundary. | Define separate entries: fume-admit permissive, control setpoint, low-temperature divert limit, and divert reset. |
| F-04 | OFF → PURGE → HEAT-UP | The purge timer is in the BPCS. The purge and light-off sequence is a combustion safeguard (NFPA 86) and belongs to the BMS. | The BPCS sends a purge request to the BMS. The BPCS then waits for BMS "purge complete" and "flame proven". Do not time the purge in the BPCS. |
| F-05 | PURGE → HEAT-UP | No light-off state. The model goes from purge to heat-up with no proven flame. | Add a LIGHT-OFF state. Its exit condition is BMS "main flame proven". |
| F-06 | OFF → PURGE | No permissives. Purge can start with XV-601 open, the fan stopped, or fuel valves not proven closed. | Add entry permissives (see T-01). |
| F-07 | Whole model | XV-602 is never mentioned. The relationship between XV-601 and XV-602 is not defined. Both closed blocks CL-6 exhaust, which risks solvent build-up in the line. Both open sends fumes to the stack untreated. | Make XV-602 position part of every state. Use sequenced make-before-break transfers with position proof. |
| F-08 | READY → PROCESS | The operator opening XV-601 from the faceplate is a device action, not a state command. There are no permissives and no check on XV-602. | Replace it with an ADMIT FUMES command that runs sequence SEQ-ADM. Lock the valve faceplates in AUTO while the RTO is in automatic states. |
| F-09 | PROCESS → COOL-DOWN | Stop goes straight to COOL-DOWN. There is no fume divert, no CL-6 handshake, and no burner shutdown step. | Route Stop through sequence SEQ-DIV (fumes to bypass), then shut the burner down, then enter COOL-DOWN. |
| F-10 | PROCESS low temperature | "Burner goes to high fire" is regulatory control placed in the state model. It is open-loop and gives no protection if high fire is not enough. Fumes stay admitted below destruction temperature, which is a permit deviation. | Put temperature control in a PID loop (Section 4). Add an automatic PROCESS → READY divert at the low-temperature divert limit. |
| F-11 | PROCESS high temperature | Not addressed. High solvent loading can drive self-sustaining combustion and over-temperature. | Reference the high-temperature trip in the C&E chart and the BMS SRS. Add a high-temperature response as an open item (hot-gas bypass or dilution air). |
| F-12 | "Any state to FAULT: any trip" | "Any trip" is not defined. Transition from OFF to FAULT is meaningless. The response in FAULT is not stated (fuel, fan, fumes). | Define TRIPPED entry by reference to the C&E chart. State the safe condition. Separate BMS trips (fuel off) from process trips. |
| F-13 | FAULT | No exit. The system cannot recover. | Add exit TRIPPED → COOL-DOWN or OFF on operator reset, with the cause cleared. Never restart the burner automatically. |
| F-14 | Missing transitions | No Stop from PURGE, LIGHT-OFF, HEAT-UP, or READY. No PROCESS → READY (hot standby during a line stop). | Add these transitions (see the transition table). |
| F-15 | All transitional states | No timeouts. Heat-up or cool-down can hang forever. | Add a timeout and failure response to each one. |
| F-16 | Whole model | Bad PV, comms loss, power loss and restart, and fail positions are not defined. A single TT-601 is used for permit compliance and for control. | Add Section 8. Raise an open item for redundant TT-601 or voting. |
| F-17 | Whole model | No CL-6 interface. CL-6 does not know whether the RTO is available. | Add an "RTO-6 available for fumes" signal to CL-6 and a CL-6 "exhaust running" signal to RTO-6. |
| F-18 | Whole model | Burner and fan have no tags. Tags for the RTO bed switching valves are missing. | Assign tags from the instrument index. |
| F-19 | Whole model | No initiator or automation level per transition (ISA-106). | Add both columns. |

## Corrected State Model

### 1. Purpose and boundaries

RTO-6 destroys solvent fumes from CL-6. Upstream is the CL-6 exhaust header. Downstream is the stack. XV-602 sends fumes to the stack untreated.

The BMS owns purge, ignition, flame supervision, and the fuel safety shutoff valves. The BPCS requests BMS actions and monitors BMS status. The BPCS does not override the BMS.

### 2. Equipment and tags

See the instrument index, document number TBD (OI-01).

Tags used here: XV-601, XV-602, TT-601. Tags to be assigned: burner (BR-601), combustion fan (K-601), BMS status signals.

### 3. States

| ID | State | Burner | K-601 | XV-601 | XV-602 | Allowed exits |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FR-RTO6-001 | OFF | Off, fuel valves closed (BMS) | Off | Closed | Open | PURGE |
| FR-RTO6-002 | PURGE | Off (BMS purging) | Running, airflow proven | Closed | Open | LIGHT-OFF, OFF, TRIPPED |
| FR-RTO6-003 | LIGHT-OFF | Trial for ignition (BMS) | Running | Closed | Open | HEAT-UP, OFF, TRIPPED |
| FR-RTO6-004 | HEAT-UP | Firing, TIC-601 in AUTO at the heat-up ramp | Running | Closed | Open | READY, COOL-DOWN, TRIPPED |
| FR-RTO6-005 | READY (hot standby) | Firing, TIC-601 in AUTO | Running | Closed | Open | PROCESS (via SEQ-ADM), COOL-DOWN, TRIPPED |
| FR-RTO6-006 | PROCESS | Firing or low fire, TIC-601 in AUTO | Running | Open | Closed | READY (via SEQ-DIV), COOL-DOWN (via SEQ-DIV), TRIPPED |
| FR-RTO6-007 | COOL-DOWN | Off, fuel valves closed (BMS) | Running | Closed | Open | OFF, TRIPPED |
| FR-RTO6-008 | TRIPPED | Off (BMS trip, or BPCS fuel cutback by C&E) | Per C&E: running for cool-down unless a fan fault | Closed (fail action) | Open (fail action) | COOL-DOWN, OFF |

**Test method for 001–008:** At FAT, put the system into each state. Verify the device positions and modes against this table.

### 3a. Transitions

| ID | From → To | Initiator | Condition / permissive | Automation level | Timeout (setpoint list) | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T-01 / FR-RTO6-010 | OFF → PURGE | Operator: START | XV-601 closed proven. XV-602 open proven. BMS ready. No active trip. TT-601 not bad. | Operator-prompted | — | Start rejected. HMI shows the missing permissive. |
| T-02 / FR-RTO6-011 | PURGE → LIGHT-OFF | Auto | BMS "purge complete" | Automatic | Purge timeout | Go to OFF. Alarm. |
| T-03 / FR-RTO6-012 | LIGHT-OFF → HEAT-UP | Auto | BMS "main flame proven" | Automatic | Light-off timeout | Go to TRIPPED (BMS lockout). |
| T-04 / FR-RTO6-013 | HEAT-UP → READY | Auto | TT-601 above the fume-admit permissive for the hold time | Automatic | Heat-up timeout | Alarm. Stay in HEAT-UP. Operator selects STOP or extends. |
| T-05 / FR-RTO6-014 | READY → PROCESS | Operator: ADMIT FUMES | TT-601 above the fume-admit permissive. CL-6 exhaust running. Flame proven. No inlet LEL alarm (OI-05). | Operator-prompted; runs SEQ-ADM | See SEQ-ADM | See SEQ-ADM |
| T-06 / FR-RTO6-015 | PROCESS → READY | Operator: DIVERT, or Auto: TT-601 below the low-temperature divert limit, or CL-6 exhaust stopped | — | Automatic or operator; runs SEQ-DIV | See SEQ-DIV | See SEQ-DIV |
| T-07 / FR-RTO6-016 | PROCESS → COOL-DOWN | Operator: STOP | — | Operator-prompted; runs SEQ-DIV, then burner off request to BMS | See SEQ-DIV | See SEQ-DIV |
| T-08 / FR-RTO6-017 | HEAT-UP or READY → COOL-DOWN | Operator: STOP | — | Operator-prompted | — | — |
| T-09 / FR-RTO6-018 | PURGE or LIGHT-OFF → OFF | Operator: STOP | — | Operator-prompted | — | — |
| T-10 / FR-RTO6-019 | COOL-DOWN → OFF | Auto | TT-601 below the cool-down complete limit | Automatic | Cool-down timeout | Alarm. K-601 stays running. |
| T-11 / FR-RTO6-020 | Any state except OFF → TRIPPED | Auto | Any cause in the C&E chart for RTO-6 (OI-02) | Automatic | — | Fail actions per Section 8 |
| T-12 / FR-RTO6-021 | TRIPPED → COOL-DOWN | Operator: RESET | Cause cleared. K-601 available. TT-601 above the cool-down complete limit. | Operator-prompted | — | Reset rejected. HMI shows the cause. |
| T-13 / FR-RTO6-022 | TRIPPED → OFF | Operator: RESET | Cause cleared. TT-601 below the cool-down complete limit, or K-601 not available. | Operator-prompted | — | Reset rejected. HMI shows the cause. |

**Test method for 010–022:** Force each condition at FAT. Verify the target state, the timeout action, and the rejection message.

### 4. Regulatory control

**FR-RTO6-030, TIC-601**

- PV: TT-601.
- Output: burner firing rate demand to the BMS.
- Action: reverse.
- In HEAT-UP, the setpoint follows the heat-up ramp in the setpoint list.
- In READY and PROCESS, the setpoint is the operating setpoint in the setpoint list.
- In OFF, COOL-DOWN, and TRIPPED, the output goes to the minimum and the loop goes to MAN.
- The BMS limits the firing rate. The BPCS cannot override the BMS.
- No tuning values are given here.

This replaces the "high fire" rule.

**FR-RTO6-031, inlet pressure control for the CL-6 header**

Inlet pressure control by K-601 speed or a damper is needed. Tag and loop are TBD (OI-04).

### 5. Sequences

**SEQ-ADM: admit fumes (make-before-break)**

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Command XV-601 open. | XV-601 open proven | XV-601 stroke timeout | Close XV-601. Stay in READY. Alarm. |
| 2 | Command XV-602 closed. | XV-602 closed proven | XV-602 stroke timeout | Open XV-602. Close XV-601. Stay in READY. Alarm. |
| 3 | Set "fumes treated" to CL-6. Enter PROCESS. | — | — | — |

**SEQ-DIV: divert fumes (make-before-break)**

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Command XV-602 open. | XV-602 open proven | XV-602 stroke timeout | Go to TRIPPED. Signal CL-6 to stop the exhaust source (OI-06). |
| 2 | Command XV-601 closed. | XV-601 closed proven | XV-601 stroke timeout | Go to TRIPPED. Alarm. |
| 3 | Clear "fumes treated" to CL-6. Enter READY or COOL-DOWN, per the command. | — | — | — |

**Test method:** At FAT, simulate a stroke failure at each step. Verify the failure response. Also verify that XV-601 and XV-602 are never both closed.

### 6. Interlocks and permissives

See the C&E chart for RTO-6 (OI-02). Burner safety functions are in the BMS SRS (OI-03). This narrative does not restate them.

### 7. Alarms

See the rationalized alarm database for RTO-6.

### 8. Abnormal handling

| ID | Condition | Response |
|---|---|---|
| FR-RTO6-040 | TT-601 bad PV | In PROCESS: run SEQ-DIV to READY. TIC-601 goes to MAN at its last output. Alarm. Block T-04 and T-05. |
| FR-RTO6-041 | BPCS–BMS comms loss | Run SEQ-DIV. Alarm. The BMS keeps its own protection. |
| FR-RTO6-042 | BPCS–CL-6 comms loss | Clear "fumes treated". Run SEQ-DIV. Alarm. |
| FR-RTO6-043 | Power loss and restart | Restart in OFF, or in TRIPPED if a cause is still active. Never restart the burner automatically. Operator must select START. |
| FR-RTO6-044 | Fail positions | XV-601 fails closed. XV-602 fails open. XV-602 stroke time must not be slower than XV-601 (OI-07). |
| FR-RTO6-045 | Instrument air loss | Valves go to fail positions. Fumes go to the stack. Go to TRIPPED. |

### 9. Operator interface

FR-RTO6-050: The RTO-6 faceplate gives these commands: START, ADMIT FUMES, DIVERT, STOP, RESET.

The HMI shows:

- the current state
- the step in the active sequence
- each missing permissive
- the active trip cause

XV-601 and XV-602 faceplates are locked in AUTO in all states except OFF. Operations must sign off these prompts (OI-08).
